text.p: Programme of soccer matches in the German first division this weekend.

Relegation-threatened Rostock have won their last three home games but may struggle to make it four in a row after suffering a 5-1 thrashing at Stuttgart last week. Moenchengladbach revitalised under new trainer Hannes Bongartz but have collected only eight points all season from away games.

Duisburg riding high after 5-2 defeat of Cologne followed by 3-2 win over champions Dortmund in their last two games. Duesseldorf have lost four of their last five matches and will be without injured libero Joerg Bach.

Battle of two of Bundesliga's strongest candidates for a UEFA Cup place. The sides drew 2-2 in the first half of the season but home advantage may give 1860 the edge this time. The Munich side have won all of their last five home games.

Bottom-of-the-table Freiburg already planning for second division soccer next season but St Pauli still hoping to avoid the drop. St Pauli striker Jens Scharping returns to squad after injury. Freiburg forward Michael Sternkopf carrying slight ankle injury but still expected to play.

Karlsruhe coach Winfried Schaefer under pressure following 3-0 defeat to regional league side Energie Cottbus Tuesday's Cup semifinal. Four key players doubtful for Bremen -- striker Bruno Labbadia, international midfielder Jens Todt, forward Bernd Hobsch and utility player Thomas Wolter.

Both sides going through bad patch of form. Schalke suffering from strains of UEFA Cup campaign, face Tenerife in second leg of their semifinal on Tuesday. Hamburg perilously close to relegation zone and their only hope of European competetion disappeared on Wednesday when they lost Cup semifinal to Stuttgart.

Cologne coach Peter Neururer under pressure without a win in seven games, even though he rescued Cologne from relegation less than a year ago. Bielefeld without a win in their last five matches. Both striker Uwe Fuchs and defender Silvio Meissner unable to train for Bielefeld because of a stomach bug.

Dortmund set to welcome back Juergen Kohler, Karlheinz Riedle and libero Matthias Sammer from suspension in match they cannot afford to lose if they are serious about winning third title in a row. Playmaker Andreas Moeller has also recovered from heavy 'flu and should play. Thomas Strunz is the only major injury worry for Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni.

Stuttgart starting to dream of the double after beating Hamburg in Wednesday's Cup semifinal. Leverkusen coach Christoph Daum says he would be happy with a point but has question marks over fitness of key players such as striker Ulf Kirsten and captain Jens Nowotny.
